title: Markets Reprice to the Fed's First Rate Hike Since 2023 as Inflation Reaccelerates
content:
The window's defining shift was the abandonment of the rate-cut framing that had underpinned the summer, as reaccelerating inflation and Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish message forced traders to confront an outright hike rather than a cut. Warsh signalled the decision would hinge on the data, and the data obliged.

August CPI sealed it: headline rose 0.4% on the month and held at **3.4%** year-on-year, with core topping forecasts. Fed funds futures swung from roughly even odds towards near-certainty, around **89%**, of a 25bp move at the 15-16 September FOMC, driving a pronounced **hawkish repricing** that lifted the 2-year yield and pushed the dollar index to about **99**.

The move rippled across every asset: front-end yields firmed, the dollar strengthened and non-yielding assets came under pressure. With a first hike since 2023 in view, the dot plot and any hint of a second move became the market's central obsession.

title: Global Long-End Bond Rout Deepens on Fiscal Strain and Rising Term Premium
content:
Running alongside the Fed story was a worldwide sell-off in long-dated government debt, as investors demanded a higher **term premium** for swelling deficits, sticky inflation and reduced central-bank support. The long end led lower, a persistent theme that reinforced week after week.

The US 30-year pushed past **5.25%** and the 10-year touched a cycle high near **4.97%**, while Germany's 10-year reached its highest since 2011, Japan's 10-year cleared **3%** for the first time in roughly three decades, and the UK sold 30-year gilts near **5.82%**, a record auction yield. US federal debt topping 40 trillion dollars sharpened the fiscal unease.

The rout mattered because it lifted discount rates globally, pressuring equities and housing-sensitive sectors and signalling that fiscal, not just monetary, forces were now steering the curve. Supply and auctions became the swing factor.

title: Middle East Oil Shock Reignites Inflation and Feeds the Bond Sell-Off
content:
A renewed escalation in the Middle East delivered an oil-price shock that reignited inflation fears and connected the window's other themes. What began as shipping disruption hardened into a broad **supply shock** as the conflict intensified through the period.

Brent pushed above **$100** for the first time since July, settling around **$101** after US strikes on Iranian tankers and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia raised fears over the Strait of Hormuz. US pump prices climbed to roughly **$4.22** a gallon, and gasoline did much of the heavy lifting in the hot August CPI print.

The shock mattered because it was the causal spark linking geopolitics to inflation, bonds and central-bank expectations, hardening the case for a Fed hike and higher yields. Any Hormuz disruption remained the key tail risk to watch.

title: AI-Led Equities Set Records Before a Rate-Driven Pullback
content:
US equities' engine stayed the AI complex, which powered indices to fresh records early in the window before rising rates forced a retreat. Breadth remained narrow, leaving benchmarks unusually reliant on a handful of megacap names.

The S&P 500 struck a peak near **7,814** as Nvidia's results reaffirmed relentless **AI capex**, with guidance pointing to revenue growth around **70%**, dragging chip peers higher. The advance stalled as the hawkish rate repricing and the bond rout lifted yields and the dollar, sending the index down four straight sessions towards **7,657** before a modest bounce.

The episode mattered because it exposed the clash between AI-driven earnings strength and richer discount rates. With tech leadership the decisive swing factor for broad indices, the September FOMC loomed as the next test of the rally's resilience.
